content: H3N8 is a specific subtype of the Influenza A virus, which is sometimes referred to as the bird flu virus. This particular subtype has become endemic in several species, including birds, horses, and dogs. There is evidence suggesting that H3N8 may have been responsible for causing a human pandemic either in 1889 or in 1900. However, there is some disagreement among sources, as some attribute the 1889 pandemic to the H2N2 subtype instead. Experts also differ in their level of certainty regarding whether H3N8 or H2N2 was definitively involved in either of these pandemics. Additionally, H3N8 was identified as the subtype responsible for more than 25% of influenza infections in wild ducks, as observed in a study conducted in 1997.
